rubrics.criterion: The non-interactive runner selection obtains the selected runner identity from the shared runner identity definition (for example by selecting its existing enum members or equivalent owner-provided values) instead of writing raw 'npm'/'yarn' literals re-typed to the runner option type at the flag-mapping site.
rubrics.rationale: This instance asks for package-manager knowledge to be owned in one place; the non-interactive flag path is the first of the two runner-selection stages the solver must reroute through that owner.

rubrics.criterion: The interactive prompt's runner question yields answer values taken from the shared runner identity definition (its enum members or equivalent owner-provided values), so no raw runner literal is locally re-typed into the runner option type inside the prompting stage.
rubrics.rationale: The interactive path is the second, independent birthplace of runner identity in this CLI (it never executes the flag-mapping site the non-interactive path uses); consolidating only one of the two entrances would leave the scatter in place.

rubrics.criterion: The dependency-installation step chooses the spawned package-manager command and its arguments via the shared runner identity (enum-member dispatch, owner-provided data, or another owner-routed design), leaving no per-module registry keyed by raw runner names in the module that performs installation.
rubrics.rationale: In the injected state, the install step consults a module-local { npm: [...], yarn: [] } arguments table - a private copy of runner dispatch data - so a sound repair must route this decision through the consolidated owner rather than merely reformatting the table.

rubrics.criterion: Inside the generated-project adaptation flow, runner-specific decisions (which project gets the yarn-specific script override, and which lockfile the .gitignore entry names) are driven by the shared runner identity / owner-provided values, with no module-level tables keyed by raw runner names and no comparison of a runner value against a raw runner literal.
rubrics.rationale: The project-generation stage is the output boundary of this instance's runner knowledge: it currently carries two raw-keyed registries plus a raw 'yarn' comparison guarding the lockfile replacement, so its rewiring is the deepest part of the consolidation.

rubrics.criterion: After the rework, the module that defines the runner identity is the only CLI module that encodes runner-specific facts (which package managers exist and their per-runner implications such as install arguments, generated-script overrides, and ignored lockfiles); every other CLI module only consumes that knowledge, so extending or renaming the supported runner set would not require synchronized edits across several lifecycle stages.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's core shotgun-surgery outcome stated in the task prompt ('adding, renaming, or otherwise changing a supported package manager is a small, local change'); a repair that only removes some fragments while leaving runner facts in two or more modules does not resolve it.

rubrics.criterion: The runner-typed option pipeline is preserved end to end: the selection, prompting, installation, and generation stages still exchange the runner value through the shared runner type (imports and type references adjusted accordingly), without widening the exchanged runner value to an ad-hoc string/boolean in any stage.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation must rewire consumption, not dissolve the typed contract: the runner type already exists and is the natural channel from owner to consumers, and keeping it is what makes the single-owner design continue to type-check under this repository's strict TypeScript configuration.

rubrics.criterion: Every runner fact removed from a consuming stage is still in effect at its point of use after the rework: installation still consults per-runner arguments for the spawned command, and generation still applies the yarn-specific script override and the per-runner .gitignore lockfile entry through the consolidated source.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible solver failure is deleting the scattered tables without reconnecting the data (silently dropping the yarn script override or lockfile swap); this item checks the ripped-out knowledge was relocated into the owner and re-consumed, not just removed.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidated runner knowledge ends up with the owner the task points at - the runner identity's own definition - and is not merely regrouped inside some other single module, such as the CLI's entry-point/composition module or a new module created beside the consumers that leaves the identity definition orphaned.
rubrics.rationale: A tempting shortcut is to gather the raw runner facts into one new pile next to their consumers (or into the composition root) and leave the existing runner identity definition unrelated; that reduces the match count but still forces a future maintainer to consult two unrelated places, which is the failure mode observed when this case was first assembled.

rubrics.criterion: No vestige of the injected per-module runner knowledge is left behind: no unreferenced raw-keyed runner table or orphaned fragment of one, no leftover literal-to-runner re-typing, and no dead branch still dispatching on a raw runner literal.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving an orphaned registry or cast in a module would keep a stale copy of runner knowledge in the codebase - exactly the drift this instance's maintainer narrative complains about - even if the live path no longer uses it.

rubrics.criterion: The CLI's non-interactive surface is unchanged: no flag, default, or help/usage text differs from before, npm remains the default runner, and the yarn flag still selects yarn.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt pins the flag surface because the integration behavior of this repository's CLI (argument parsing specs and usage output) depends on those exact flags, defaults, and text.

rubrics.criterion: The interactive prompt still asks the same runner question with the same choice labels in the same 'npm' then 'yarn' order, and the returned answer still selects the corresponding runner.
rubrics.rationale: Runner-choice presentation is user-visible behavior quoted in the prompt's stability list; a repair that reassigned, relabeled, or reordered the choices would change the interactive experience this instance requires to be preserved.

rubrics.criterion: Dependency installation still invokes the same package-manager command with the same effective arguments as before (npm with its install argument, yarn as a bare install) and keeps the same failure handling.
rubrics.rationale: Moving install arguments into the consolidated owner must not alter the spawned process: this repository's execa-based install path normalizes certain call shapes, so a repair that swaps call forms must still produce the identical effective command.

rubrics.criterion: Generated projects are byte-identical for both runners: package.json content and scripts (only yarn projects carry the yarn-specific script override, with unchanged key presence/ordering) and the .gitignore lockfile entry (yarn projects replace 'yarn.lock' with the other runner's lockfile; npm projects keep the template entry) are exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: This repository verifies generation via md5 fingerprints of the files produced in sandboxed end-to-end runs, so any byte-level drift in the adapted template files would fail behavior preservation for this instance even though the runner knowledge itself was consolidated correctly.

rubrics.criterion: The rework stays within the CLI area: the library sources, their public export surface, and the template files the CLI ships to generated projects are not edited.
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt scopes this instance to the CLI modules precisely because the library and templates are consumed by generated projects; edits there would leak the restructuring into unrelated public surface or into project generation output.
